# Kloudbean

> Kloudbean is a managed cloud hosting platform that runs your whole application stack from one dashboard: application servers, managed databases, S3-compatible object storage, static sites, and a built-in load balancer. It provisions on seven cloud providers (AWS, AWS Lightsail, Google Cloud, Linode, Vultr, DigitalOcean, UpCloud) and has been shipping since November 2023. Applications run always-on as persistent processes, not scale-to-zero serverless functions, so there are no cold starts. Pricing is flat, starting at $8/mo, and egress is not metered.

Kloudbean is built for teams that want managed infrastructure without becoming full-time infrastructure operators. It suits Node.js APIs and backends, PHP and WordPress sites, Python, Ruby, and Java applications, static sites, and enterprise or government workloads that need in-house-team support.

## What Kloudbean provides

- Cloud providers (7): AWS, AWS Lightsail, Google Cloud (GCP), Linode, Vultr, DigitalOcean, UpCloud. You choose the provider and region at launch.
- Managed databases (one-click, with automatic backups and controlled access): PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, Memcached, Elasticsearch.
- Application runtimes: Node.js (Express, NestJS, Fastify, Next.js, React, Vue, Angular; PM2 multi-process supported), Python (Django, Flask, FastAPI), Ruby, Java, PHP (WordPress, WooCommerce, Laravel, Magento, Drupal, Joomla).
- Always-on processes: applications run persistently under PM2. No spin-down, no cold starts, and background workers and WebSocket connections run on the same server.
- Object storage: S3-compatible buckets with AWS SDK and CLI compatibility, plus managed Google Cloud Storage buckets.
- Static site hosting: free, with custom domains, SSL, and built-in visit analytics.
- Flexible Load Balancer (FLB): built in and available to enable on any account, with virtual load balancers, application pools, SSL management, and access logs.
- Managed CI/CD: connect a Git repository (GitHub, including GitHub OAuth) and build and deploy on every push, with deployment history and live build logs.
- Security baseline: Shorewall firewall and Fail2ban applied automatically, free SSL, Basic Auth gating for apps, IP access control with CIDR support, HttpOnly cookie sessions.
- Team controls: subusers with granular per-resource, per-action User Access Control (UAC), plus social login via Google, GitHub, and LinkedIn.
- Operations: cron jobs from the dashboard without SSH, staging sites for WordPress and Laravel, automatic backups, runtime configuration for Node and Python in the UI, and a read-only Platform API with scoped personal tokens.
- One-click smart and AI apps: n8n, Supabase, OpenWebUI with DeepSeek, Postiz, Penpot.
- Enterprise only: Kubernetes, autoscaling, custom architectures, VPC and private networking, and an immutable account-wide Audit Trail with CSV export.

## Pricing model

- Flat plans starting at $8/mo. The plan covers the server running your application and its processes.
- Egress and bandwidth are not metered, so traffic spikes and bot traffic do not create usage-based invoices.
- Managed databases, object storage, and the load balancer are provisioned in the same account and dashboard as the application.
- A free trial is available, and free migration assistance is included for moving an existing application across.
- Cloudflare is available as a paid add-on for all sites, and is free for Enterprise accounts.

## Scope and boundaries

- Kloudbean runs Linux stacks: PHP, Node.js, Python, Ruby, Java, and their databases. It does not host Windows, .NET Framework, or IIS workloads.
- "Managed" covers the server, stack, SSL, backups, and patching. You own your application code and your data.
- Compliance is shared: the platform provides infrastructure controls, and the customer owns application-level compliance.
- Kubernetes, autoscaling, VPC, and Audit Trail are Enterprise features and are not part of standard accounts. Kloudbean does not autoscale a standard account's application automatically.
- Kloudbean runs persistent always-on processes. It is not a scale-to-zero serverless platform.
